NOTES ON THE PURSUIT

STAY IN
MOTION.

Three perspectives on the everyday practice of doing. Open a chapter and take what stays with you.

01 / INTENTIONSTART BEFORE
YOU’RE READY.

There is a particular kind of waiting that feels like preparation. One more plan. A better day. A clearer reason.

Beginning doesn’t need to be dramatic. It can be a single honest action, small enough to do today. The first draft. The first lap. The first time you choose to show up for yourself.

You can decide what comes next after you begin.

02 / CONSISTENCYTHE QUIET
REPETITIONS.

Most meaningful work happens without an audience. The ordinary days rarely make the story, but they are the story.

Build a rhythm you can return to. Let effort be something you practice, not something you perform. Progress doesn’t need to look impressive to be real.

The next repetition is enough for now.

03 / PERSPECTIVELEAVE ROOM
TO RESET.

Forward isn’t always faster. Sometimes it means stepping back far enough to notice what the rush has hidden.

Make room for the pause. Reconsider the route. A deliberate return can say more than another hour of going through the motions.

Begin again, with a little more intention.
